transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-01-07 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Soto (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Ellen Marsh (Head of IT - Lyceum), Marco Ruiz (DevOps), Leah Cohen (PM)

Summary:
Quick security posture scoping: Lyceum evaluates hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for inference workloads (clinical notes summarization). Primary concerns: data residency, KMS integration/HSM, audit logs retention, SAML SSO + attribute mapping, fine-grained RBAC, SOC2/ISO evidence, and deletion/retention workflows. They want a pilot on Dedicated with KMS-backed keys and audit log export to their Splunk.

Topics covered:
- SOC2/ISO deliverables and timelines
- SSO/SAML attributes and IdP mapping
- RBAC roles and admin workflows
- Audit logs: fields, retention, export, tamper-evidence
- Encryption: in transit, at rest, customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS)
- Data retention & deletion (GDPR/clinical data constraints)
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: All right thanks for doing this, Ellen, Marco, Leah — quick intro from our side. I'm Alex, AE, and Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya: Hi everyone, Priya Nair. We'll focus this call on security gating items so we can map your constraints to Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private options.
[00:20] Ellen: Great, we got a list from procurement. Primary use case is clinical summarization, PHI-ish, so compliance is the big driver.
[00:28] Marco: Uh and a lot of egress controls, we need audit trails pushed into our Splunk cluster and keys managed centrally via our KMS.
[00:36] Leah: Also timeline: we want a pilot in Q1, production by end of Q2 if everything checks out.
[00:44] Alex: Understood. Quick Q — do you already have SOC2 or ISO needs documented?
[00:47] Ellen: SOC2 Type II will be required for vendor. We also have to map ISO27001 controls for our internal auditors.
[00:53] Priya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we can provide the report; we also have an ISO attestation in process, we'll share artifacts. For keys we support customer-managed KMS across Hosted and Dedicated — and HSM-backed keys for Private.
[01:12] Marco: When you say Hosted with customer-managed keys, is that like a CMEK model where we hold keys in our cloud KMS?
[01:18] Priya: Yes — we support CMEK for some cloud providers, we also support a vault-proxy arrangement for Dedicated. For Private (VPC or on-prem) you get direct HSM access. There's some setup to wire our runtime to your key wrappers.
[01:31] Marco: Cool, need specifics — rotation, wrap/unwarp operations, and whether Redwood ever sees plaintext.
[01:36] Priya: Short answer: Redwood does not have access to plaintext encryption keys when you use CMEK/HSM; tokens are wrapped. We'll send the exact KMS flows.
[01:45] Ellen: Audit logs — what fields are available? We need queryable logs: request_id, user_id, model, prompt hash, token count, latency, IPs, and redaction flags.
[01:56] Alex: We emit a structured audit log for each request. You can export to syslog, S3, or push to your SIEM. Retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private; Hosted has default retention 90 days but enterprise retention add-ons available.
[02:12] Marco: Do logs include prompt content? For PHI we can't export raw prompts to Splunk without DLP.
[02:19] Priya: Good point. We support field-level redaction and can hash or truncate prompt text before export. There's also an option to keep raw content only in encrypted internal store with restricted access and only push metadata.
[02:33] Leah: For compliance we also need immutable tamper-evident logs for audit — how is that guaranteed?
[02:39] Priya: On Dedicated/Private you can write logs to append-only storage in your account or we can stream to an external WORM-compatible bucket. Hosted has signed log blobs and audit trails with provenance. We'll share the docs.
[02:54] Ellen: SSO — we use Okta; we need SAML with attribute mapping to our groups. Can Redwood map SAML attributes to RBAC roles?
[03:02] Alex: Yes, SAML SSO supported, you can map attributes into roles. Our RBAC model supports roles at org, project, and model level.
[03:11] Marco: Are there audit hooks for admin actions — who changed RBAC, who rotated keys, who created model versions?
[03:18] Priya: All admin actions are logged and surfaced in the Console. We also emit those events to external logging endpoints.
[03:25] Ellen: Data residency — our legal requires EU data residency for EU patients. How do you handle region pinning?
[03:31] Alex: We can route requests to region-specific clusters and you can pin workloads. For Dedicated we can provision in the region you need; Private gives you full control.
[03:40] Leah: On deletion — we need rights to delete patient prompts on request. Can you support per-customer deletion requests and show proof?
[03:47] Priya: Yes, we have deletion APIs and can produce deletion attestations (log + hash) for compliance. In Hosted we have a standard workflow; Dedicated/Private gives you more direct control and quicker SLAs.
[04:00] Marco: Any limitations on long-context models? We test 16k+ contexts. How does KV cache and batching behave?
[04:07] Priya: Our runtime supports long contexts; small caveat — when using quantized variants there's some perf tradeoff. Also note transcription spelled KV cache sometimes becomes KV cash in older logs, haha. We'll provide perf profiles for 16k and 32k contexts.
[04:21] Alex: Quick commercial note — Dedicated pilot pricing can include ingress/egress allowances; Private has setup fees for HSM certs.
[04:29] Leah: Procurement will need SOX-ish paperwork and vendor contracts — timeline?
[04:33] Alex: We can start standard NDA and MSAs; we'll send template and our procurement packet after this.
[04:40] Ellen: Backup and snapshots — where are model artifacts and logs backed up? We need S3 replicas in our account.
[04:47] Priya: On Dedicated/Private we can snapshot into your S3 buckets. Hosted stores backups in our environment but can be configured to replicate to your buckets for retention.
[04:56] Marco: For crypto, are keys rotated automatically or manual? We prefer rotation every 90 days and want KMS to enforce it.
[05:03] Priya: KMS rotations are supported; rotation policies can be set in your KMS and we honor them. For HSM-backed keys you get rotation control and key material never exported.
[05:12] Leah: Does Redwood provide penetration test reports and vulnerability scanning results?
[05:16] Alex: We have pentest summaries and vulnerability scanning cadence; we can share high-level results. For deeper dives we sign an NDA.
[05:24] Ellen: Let's talk about role separation. We need strict separation between platform ops and application owners; can you create console roles that prevent DevOps from seeing prompts?
[05:33] Priya: Yes — RBAC supports fine-grained permissions (read/write/model-deploy/keys/admin). You can create least-privilege roles so DevOps can deploy infra but not view prompt payloads.
[05:44] Marco: How do you handle service accounts and API keys? We want ephemeral tokens bound to mTLS or cert-based auth ideally.
[05:52] Priya: We support short-lived tokens, scoped keys, and mTLS for Private. For Hosted we support restricted API keys and token TTLs with rotation.
[06:03] Leah: Any SLA for data deletion in Hosted? We need deletion within 48 hours for sensitive records.
[06:08] Alex: Hosted standard is 72 hours for full purge but we can negotiate a tighter SLA on enterprise plan or suggest Dedicated/Private for guaranteed 48-hour deletes.
[06:18] Ellen: What's the process for security questionnaires? We have a 3rd-party vendor assessment with a 200+ question RFP.
[06:24] Alex: We have a security questionnaire pack (pre-filled responses) and can assign a solutions contact to help with complex answers.
[06:31] Marco: Any integrations with DLP or tokenization at the edge?
[06:35] Priya: We offer inline tokenization clients and a pre-send webhook that can run your DLP rules before content hits our runtime. For Dedicated/Private you can run DLP entirely inside your VPC.
[06:47] Leah: For the pilot, what do you recommend — Hosted with CMEK or Dedicated?
[06:52] Priya: If you need rapid start and still want KMS control, Hosted+CMEK can work. But because you have strict retention and Splunk export requirements, Dedicated might be simpler and more auditable. Private if you require full HSM and air-gap.
[07:05] Ellen: We prefer Dedicated pilot but want to verify the KMS flows and Splunk ingestion first.
[07:11] Alex: Next steps recap — we'll send SOC2 + ISO docs, KMS integration guide, Splunk export spec, and proposed pilot SOW. Also schedule Priya's bench with your test prompts.
[07:23] Marco: I'll gather KMS details (vendor, key IDs, rotation policy) and test dataset.
[07:28] Leah: Procurement will want an initial term sheet and pricing for a 6-week pilot.
[07:33] Alex: We'll draft that and loop in legal.
[07:36] Ellen: Any blockers from our side? None right now — timeline looks doable.
[07:41] Alex: Great thanks all. We'll follow up via email with links.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker overlap and minor ASR errors (product names sometimes mis-typed like 'Deticated' for Dedicated).
